CHIEF COMPLAINT
Routine follow-up with chronic medical conditions and fatigue.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
61-year-old male presents for routine follow-up. Patient reports increased fatigue, describing it as feeling drained at the end of the day. He continues to ride his road bike 20-30 miles at a time, though he notes he cannot go as fast as previously and becomes tired after long rides. He used to complete 40-mile rides but is currently limited by time. He states his friend Tyler, who is older, now waits for him during rides, which bothers him. Patient is concerned about his aortic valve, which was replaced 13 years ago, noting he was told it would last approximately 8 years. He requested an echocardiogram to assess current function. His last stress test was September 9, 2019. Patient does not currently follow up at Hopkins and prefers local follow-up care. He reports pursed lip breathing during walking, which has been noted by his wife and other doctors, but denies associated wheezing. He is able to maintain most of his bike riding pace. Additionally, he notes a small nodule on his right epididymis that he discovered incidentally and wanted to have evaluated. He denies depression and reports overall happiness. Sleep is variable, typically 6-7 hours per night. He works and lectures, attempting morning workouts and swimming twice weekly at 5:45 AM. Wife reports he snores slightly but has never mentioned apneic episodes.

Patient reports increased fatigue but denies wheezing. Denies apneic episodes per wife. No other systems reviewed.
